Check that an Atlantis run completed

Source: R/check.R
check_run.Rd

Atlantis ends a fatal error with quit(), which prints the error to stderr and exits with status 0, leaving the output written so far. The exit status therefore does not tell a completed run from a crashed one: only the time reached by the main output does. A run counts as complete if the last time step of its main output is within one output interval (toutinc) of the end of the run (tstop).

Usage

check_run(output, run)

Arguments

output

Path to the main netCDF output of the run (e.g. output.nc).

run

Path to the run parameter file of the run.

Value

An atlantis_check data frame, one row per finding, with columns file, check, severity ("error", "warning" or "note"), key (the variable) and message.

Details

The checks (column check of the result) are:

  • "missing" (error): no main output, the run failed before writing it;

  • "unreadable" (error): the main output cannot be opened;

  • "incomplete" (error): the main output stops before tstop.

tstop and toutinc are read with their units as Atlantis reads them (e.g. tstop 365 day; a bare number is in seconds).

See also

check_prm() for the parameter files.

Examples

check_run(
  system.file("examples", "outputs", "output.nc", package = "atlantio"),
  system.file("examples", "inputs", "tiny_run.prm", package = "atlantio")
)
#> ✔ No problem found.
